answer: A translation market pays agents to render a fable containing the word ember. Each source passage has a signed ID that serves as the anchor for a single reward pool; a rotating panel compares blind translations, and accounts submitting the same work split that pool. A sybil operator needs to translate many fresh passages to increase income, which costs compute and review time. Panel collusion or leaked passages can still favor a farm, so reviewers reveal evidence and are assigned only after submissions close.
